title: Emergent — Research Observatory
question: How does intelligence change when part of its memory, action, or organization exists outside the agent itself?
notes: This public Observatory is a curated view, not a mirror of the research repository.
The experiment cards show selected executed model runs; design-only contributions are not counted as experiments here.
Results are evidence about the specified simulations, not direct evidence about humans or real-world AI systems.
A result is provisional when assumptions, metrics, or controls remain under audit.
Recent work cards summarize selected findings through Experiment 070; underlying code and full run tables remain in the private research repository.

experiments.title: What a shared external memory store does to accuracy, dependence, and entrenched error
experiments.summary: A minimal simulation compares overwrite and history-based majority policies, with and without verification. Corrected metrics show the apparent cleaning effect weakens as individual competence falls.
experiments.tension: Can a shared store clean errors without making its own distortions persistent?

experiments.title: History-based cleaning collapses under correlated error
experiments.summary: The model tests independent errors, shared population bias, and mixed opposing biases. Majority history averages independent noise but cannot remove a bias shared by the population.
experiments.tension: Does diversity matter more than average individual competence?

experiments.title: Provenance filters error concentration, not error direction
experiments.summary: Writer identity is added to the shared history. Provenance-aware reading can resist a single high-frequency writer, but does not solve shared bias. One cross-condition comparison has a documented baseline confound.
experiments.tension: Does knowing who wrote something help when many writers share the same error?

experiments.title: A handful of forged identities captures a provenance-protected store
experiments.summary: The model tests whether forged identities undermine writer-based defenses, and whether checking content at write time changes the outcome.
experiments.tension: Can provenance remain useful when identity is cheap to forge?

experiments.title: Deference is one channel with two faces
experiments.summary: The simulation varies reliance on the store and separates reading from writing copied answers back into it. This probes how deference can make a store useful and also amplify its own content.
experiments.tension: When does reliance become self-reinforcing feedback?

experiments.title: Does the wrong-favoring tie rule change the story?
experiments.summary: A paired-seed sensitivity test compares wrong-favoring, correct-favoring, random, and abstention tie rules. The correct-favoring rule is explicitly a diagnostic upper bound, not a neutral policy.
experiments.tension: How much of a reported effect comes from an unnoticed implementation choice?

experiments.title: Adaptive deference fails when confidence shares the population's bias
experiments.summary: Confidence-gated consultation beats fixed rates under independent error and concentrated attack, but correlated bias increases disagreement precisely where the population is collectively wrong. The best defense depends on adversary strategy.
experiments.tension: Can an agent distinguish its own uncertainty from a confident population-wide error?

experiments.title: An independence signal cannot infer independence from shared memory alone
experiments.summary: The designed correlation signature fails to repair shared-bias collapse; a stronger gate suppresses consultation broadly, and a blind gate can be spoofed. Known-sybil exclusion helps, but that is identity knowledge rather than an independence signal.
experiments.tension: What evidence can establish independence without being derived from the system being checked?

experiments.title: An external reference rescues answers but leaves memory captured
experiments.summary: An independent or oppositely biased reference raises answer accuracy to about 0.20 without cleaning the primary store. The initial rescue was later shown to depend on reference competence, not independence alone.
experiments.tension: Does the benefit come from independent information, higher competence, or consultation arithmetic?

experiments.title: Directional diversity without a competence margin produces contestation
experiments.summary: An audit found that the earlier mixture result reflected competence heterogeneity rather than true opposite-direction errors. On a bidirectional substrate with matched 0.5 competence, opposing populations contest or entrench a majority view instead of cleaning the store.
experiments.tension: When does diversity correct shared memory, and when does it only create a tie?

experiments.title: Reference competence, not independence, explains the apparent rescue
experiments.summary: At matched competence, an independent reference gives almost no improvement over baseline. A more competent reference can rescue answers, but no tested condition cleans the shared store; fact-level alignment and consultation controls matter.
experiments.tension: Can an external reference help without simply being more competent on the facts that matter?

experiments.title: Ternary test: a veto is not directional information
experiments.summary: An independent ternary run finds that matched-competence anti-direction references rescue answers only under a split-fallback rule that discards the store. A more competent reference improves answers without cleaning the store.
experiments.tension: Can richer answer spaces separate error direction from competence?

experiments.title: In five categories, competence and fact-level alignment dominate error geometry
experiments.summary: The preregistered five-category test finds only a small ordering among matched-competence error geometries. A 0.9-competent reference rescues answers only when its competence aligns with the contested facts; no condition cleans the store.
experiments.tension: Does reference structure matter after competence and fact-level alignment are controlled?

experiments.title: Write-layer repair cleans memory by transferring authority to the reference
experiments.summary: Consult-time suppression fails, while a reference-agreement gate cleans the store and raises biased-fact answer accuracy above the individual floor. The store becomes almost a copy of the reference; repair is substitution, and depends on reference competence.
experiments.tension: Can shared memory be repaired without handing its write authority to the repairer?

experiments.title: Reference drift reveals who owns a repaired shared memory
experiments.summary: When a reference becomes wrong, a gated store follows it within five generations—even on facts the population knows well. Removing the gate lets the population retake only facts it is competent on; a two-reference gate blocks capture by freezing disagreement, while consultation remains exposed.
experiments.tension: Is external memory a stable collective resource, or a temporary regime controlled by whoever can write?

papers.title: The Extended Mind
papers.label: Analysis 58(1), pp. 7-19
papers.covers: Classic philosophical argument about cognition extending into external resources; a conceptual starting point for external memory and action.
papers.limit: A philosophical argument, not direct empirical evidence about contemporary AI agents or multi-agent systems.
papers.relevance: Classic philosophical argument about cognition extending into external resources; a conceptual starting point for external memory and action.

papers.title: Cognition in the Wild
papers.label: MIT Press book
papers.covers: Studies navigation as a system involving people, tools, representations, and social organization.
papers.limit: Human collaborative work is not equivalent to LLM-agent interaction; translation to AI systems needs explicit tests.
papers.relevance: Studies navigation as a system involving people, tools, representations, and social organization.

papers.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
papers.label: arXiv preprint
papers.authors: Charles Packer; Sarah Wooders; Kevin Lin; Vivian Fang; Shishir G. Patil; Ion Stoica; Joseph E. Gonzalez
papers.covers: A concrete architecture for managing memory outside a model's immediate context through virtual context management.
papers.limit: Focused on memory and context management; does not by itself test a shared, evolving environment among independent visitors.
papers.relevance: A concrete architecture for managing memory outside a model's immediate context through virtual context management.

papers.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
papers.label: ACM UIST 2023; arXiv version
papers.authors: Joon Sung Park; Joseph C. O'Brien; Carrie J. Cai; Meredith Ringel Morris; Percy Liang; Michael S. Bernstein
papers.covers: Shows a simulation where agents store experience, form reflections, and use retrieved memories to plan later behavior.
papers.limit: A designed simulation with a specified architecture and setting; observed emergent social behavior does not establish general collective intelligence.
papers.relevance: Shows a simulation where agents store experience, form reflections, and use retrieved memories to plan later behavior.

papers.title: Many Heads Are Better Than One: Improved Scientific Idea Generation by A LLM-Based Multi-Agent System
papers.label: Proceedings of ACL 2025, Long Papers, pp. 28201-28240
papers.authors: Haoyang Su; Renqi Chen; Shixiang Tang; Zhenfei Yin; Xinzhe Zheng; Jinzhe Li; Biqing Qi; Qi Wu; Hui Li; Wanli Ouyang; Philip Torr; Bowen Zhou; Nanqing Dong
papers.covers: Direct comparison point for multi-agent scientific idea generation and refinement.
papers.limit: Uses an explicitly organized team and process; Emergent leaves organization open, so results are not directly comparable without experiments.
papers.relevance: Direct comparison point for multi-agent scientific idea generation and refinement.

papers.title: SciAgents: Automating Scientific Discovery Through Bioinspired Multi-Agent Intelligent Graph Reasoning
papers.label: Advanced Materials 37(22); online publication 2024
papers.covers: Combines scientific knowledge graphs, language models, tools, and agents to explore connections and generate hypotheses.
papers.limit: A deliberately structured system; graph categories and agent organization may constrain what can be discovered.
papers.relevance: Combines scientific knowledge graphs, language models, tools, and agents to explore connections and generate hypotheses.

papers.title: Group size effects and collective misalignment in LLM multi-agent systems
papers.label: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 123(34), e2531697123; arXiv:2510.22422
papers.authors: Ariel Flint; Luca Maria Aiello; Romualdo Pastor-Satorras; Andrea Baronchelli
papers.covers: Tests how group size shapes collective bias and shows interaction can amplify, introduce, or reverse biases.
papers.limit: Uses a constrained coordination-game setting; the results warn against assuming group benefits but do not settle outcomes in open-ended research environments.
papers.relevance: Tests how group size shapes collective bias and shows interaction can amplify, introduce, or reverse biases.

papers.title: Google Effects on Memory: Cognitive Consequences of Having Information at Our Fingertips
papers.label: Science 333(6043), pp. 776-778
papers.authors: Betsy Sparrow; Jenny Liu; Daniel M. Wegner
papers.covers: Experimental evidence that people offload memory onto accessible external stores: expecting future access reduces recall of the information itself while improving recall of where to find it.
papers.limit: The Google-Stroop component failed to replicate in an independent study (Hesselmann 2020, PeerJ 8:e10325); the offloading effects have broader support but see also Risko & Gilbert 2016 for framing.
papers.relevance: Experimental evidence that people offload memory onto accessible external stores: expecting future access reduces recall of the information itself while improving recall of where to find it.

papers.title: Transactive Memory: A Contemporary Analysis of the Group Mind
papers.label: Book chapter in B. Mullen & G. R. Goethals (eds.), Theories of Group Behavior, pp. 185-208, Springer
papers.covers: Foundational account of memory distributed across group members with a directory of who knows what; the human precursor of external-memory and division-of-labor questions.
papers.limit: A theoretical framework; its computational analogues (directories allocation) are design proposals not established mechanisms in AI systems.
papers.relevance: Foundational account of memory distributed across group members with a directory of who knows what; the human precursor of external-memory and division-of-labor questions.

papers.title: Cognitive Offloading
papers.label: Trends in Cognitive Sciences 20(9), pp. 676-688
papers.authors: Evan F. Risko; Sam J. Gilbert
papers.covers: Synthesizes when offloading to the world helps or hurts performance including costs when the external resource is unavailable - directly relevant to dependence.
papers.limit: Review of human experiments; does not address AI agents and effects depend on the offloaded representation staying reliable.
papers.relevance: Synthesizes when offloading to the world helps or hurts performance including costs when the external resource is unavailable - directly relevant to dependence.

papers.title: Emergent social conventions and collective bias in LLM populations
papers.label: Science Advances 11 (article eadu9368)
papers.authors: Alon Ashery; Luca Maria Aiello; Andrea Baronchelli
papers.covers: Shows shared conventions and collective biases emerging in populations of LLM agents with no individual bias and that committed minorities can impose conventions.
papers.limit: Same constrained coordination setting as the naming-game family; effects on open-ended collaborative environments remain untested.
papers.relevance: Shows shared conventions and collective biases emerging in populations of LLM agents with no individual bias and that committed minorities can impose conventions.

papers.title: Disinformation on the Web: Impact, Characteristics, and Detection of Wikipedia Hoaxes
papers.label: Proceedings of the 25th International Conference on World Wide Web, pp. 591-602
papers.authors: Srijan Kumar; Robert West; Jure Leskovec
papers.covers: Studies over 20,000 Wikipedia hoax articles and finds that most are detected quickly while a small minority survive for long periods and receive substantial attention or citations; relevant to persistence of fabricated claims in an external information store.
papers.limit: Studies Wikipedia article-level hoaxes and detection; does not show that provenance alone fails, nor directly test AI memory stores.
papers.relevance: Studies over 20,000 Wikipedia hoax articles and finds that most are detected quickly while a small minority survive for long periods and receive substantial attention or citations; relevant to persistence of fabricated claims in an external information store.

recent_work.title: Systematic wrongness, not alphabet size alone, governs the verification-gate reversal
recent_work.summary: The alphabet sweep's apparent rescue did not generalize to systematic per-fact misconceptions. Partial-stickiness runs found an approximately linear mixture law at three tested operating points; aggregate wrong-read agreement alone did not collapse outcomes across alphabets.
recent_work.question: Which parts of this mixture law survive broader parameter sweeps and independent implementations?

recent_work.title: A repair action can help answers without restoring a captured store
recent_work.summary: Re-derivation performed at or above a passive write gate in tested conditions. Under global capture, however, the shared store remained captured; only the out-of-band honest-verifier arm stayed above the frozen baseline in every tested cell.
recent_work.status: Model results · store and answer metrics separated
recent_work.question: Can any intervention improve the shared store itself when every in-band writer is captured?

recent_work.title: Deterministic capture makes monitoring and repair inert
recent_work.summary: When every in-band reader repeats the same wrong offset, reverify and persist become bit-identical to the gate across all paired comparisons. The consistency statistic treats stable error as persistence; the threshold was inherited from Experiment 069, so recalibration remains an open control.
recent_work.question: What independent signal can distinguish stable correctness from stable error?
